The National Weather Service has issued a Coastal Flood Advisory for Orange County coastal communities through 5:00 PM Wednesday, September 30.

High tides and elevated surf may cause minor coastal flooding, erosion, strong rip currents, and hazardous swimming conditions.

Residents and visitors should use caution near beaches and low-lying coastal areas, avoid flooded roadways, and follow guidance from local officials and lifeguards.

My office will continue to monitor conditions and share relevant updates. Please follow guidance from local officials and lifeguards and take appropriate precautions to stay safe.

text:
One year ago, while gathering to worship, parishioners at the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints in Grand Blanc suffered an unimaginable terror attack. I join the community in remembering the four victims, extending our prayers to their families and fellow congregants, and standing with the community as we remember the tragedies of that day.

Today, we also honor the heroic first responders who were on the scene in a matter of seconds. The remarkable speed and decision-making of our 911 dispatchers, law enforcement officers, firefighters, and paramedics saved lives.

In the days, weeks, and months since, neighbors have come together to grieve, heal, and find the light under the motto, “Grand Blanc, Better Together.” In the wake of an unimaginable tragedy, the Church and its community have shown us the power of faith and hope. As they break ground tonight, all of mid-Michigan will be behind them with love and support.

text:
Five years ago, the City of San José confronted an ugly chapter in our history and apologized for the violent victimization of Chinese immigrants in San José, and for the officially-sanctioned discrimination of them and their descendants.

Last weekend, I joined the Chinese Historical and Cultural Project to mark that anniversary and celebrate 35 years of the Chinese American Historical Museum.  In my speech, I celebrated those courageous Bay Area Chinese-Americans—such as Wong Kim Ark, Mary Tape, and Lee Yick—who fought to ensure that America kept its commitment to our Constitution.

Thank you to Gerrye Wong and generations of community leaders who keep this history alive.

text:
ROAD TO 250: Founders Close to Home

Before Roslyn was Roslyn, it was Hempstead Harbor — and Hendrick Onderdonk helped shape the community we know today.

Onderdonk settled here in 1752, operated the local grist mill and built Long Island’s first paper mill in 1773. During the Revolution, his property experienced the hardships of the British occupation, and his paper mill was part of a network used to pass secret wartime messages.

Years later, on April 24, 1790, President George Washington stopped at Onderdonk’s home during his tour of Long Island and wrote about his thriving mills.

More than 235 years later, the house where Washington stopped still stands on Old Northern Boulevard in Roslyn — today home to Hendrick’s Tavern.

It’s a place many of us know, with a history we may not: another reminder that the story of America’s founding is also part of our own local history.

text:
ROAD TO 250: Founding Stories Close to Home

You don’t have to travel far to find a connection to America’s founding.

In 1790, President George Washington stopped in what is now Roslyn to visit Hendrick Onderdonk, a prominent local businessman who operated a grist mill and built Long Island’s first paper mill.

Onderdonk and his family had lived through the British occupation of Long Island, and his paper mill was part of a network used to carry secret messages during the Revolution.

The best part? The house where Washington stopped is still there today — now Hendrick’s Tavern on Old Northern Boulevard.

Our local history is American history.

text:
I was pleased to announce $1.47 billion in projected federal transportation funding that will help move important transportation projects forward in Webb County. 

Currently, $1 billion now supports 94 transportation projects across the county. This represents more than three-quarters of the total transportation funding programmed for Webb County under the 10-year plan. It will support improvements along I-35, US 59, US 83, Loop 20 and other critical roadways, including highway widening, reconstruction, new interchanges, safety improvements and bridge projects.

These federal dollars will help keep traffic moving, support international trade and improve the roads that families, businesses and commercial vehicles rely on every day, strengthening Webb County’s role as a major transportation and trade hub.

I’ll continue working to bring federal transportation dollars back home to South Texas and make sure our rapidly growing communities have the infrastructure they need to keep Webb County moving forward.

text:
I find myself agreeing with Senator Collins on this issue. This administration continues to blatantly steal from the American people.

Every single constitutional conservative should be livid at this executive overreach and I eagerly await action from the Majority on this issue. https://t.co/hKYxLTNXIB

quoted.text:
Without warning or consultation, Congress just received an $810 million package of pocket rescissions from the Administration.  This is the most recent attempt by this Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to undermine Congress’s Constitutional power of the purse. 
 
This move shows that OMB intentionally withheld these funds for months to execute this unlawful cancellation of appropriations that were approved on a bipartisan basis and signed into law.  
  
Not only is the delay itself an impoundment that was not reported to Congress, but also it is a usurpation of Congress’s appropriations powers.  OMB is an agency of the executive branch.  It does not get to decide which programs are worth funding.
 
The independent Government Accountability Office has concluded that pocket rescissions are unlawful and not permitted by the Impoundment Control Act. Any effort to rescind appropriated funds without congressional approval is a clear violation of the law.
 
I will work with my colleagues to address these illegal actions.

The independent Government Accountability Office has concluded that pocket rescissions are unlawful and not permitted by the Impoundment Control Act. Any effort to rescind appropriated funds without congressional approval is a clear violation of the law.
 
I will work with my colleagues to address these illegal actions.

One year ago, a man drove his car into the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints in Grand Blanc, set fire to it, and started shooting. People were shielding children. Four people were killed and several were injured. 

This is never easy for any community, and I remember the feeling on the ground, and how raw Michiganders felt. But I'm glad the community is working to turn the page and the church is now rebuilding its space. 

Today, we remember the lives lost and all the first responders and volunteers who responded immediately to help those in need. 

We have an epidemic in this country as there continue to be threats and deadly attacks targeting churches and other houses of worship across America. People should be able to worship without fear of being attacked.

text:
It was a pleasure to attend the 43rd annual Nargis Dutt Foundation fundraiser, which raises money for people with cancer who cannot afford care.

This is a season of festivals in the Indian American community:

Ganesh helps overcome obstacles, as the good works of this charity have.

Navratri reminds us of the importance of strength and courage, like the many victims of cancer must exhibit.

text:
Gas prices are soaring nationwide, and families feel it every time they fill up. So what does the Trump administration do? It guts the fuel economy standards that help Americans burn less gas in the first place. 

That means more money out of your pocket at the pump for years to come.

Congress created these standards in 1975, after an oil embargo showed how dangerous it is to depend on volatile foreign oil. Fifty years later, with Trump’s unauthorized war in Iran pushing prices higher, he’s forgetting that lesson entirely.

Meanwhile, the rest of the world is moving fast. 

EV sales are surging globally, and China already has dramatically accelerated the production of electric cars and batteries. Every year we pull back is another year Chinese automakers pull further ahead and American workers fall further behind.

I want American companies building the cars of the future, right here, with American workers and American innovation. 

Walking away from that race is a ridiculous self own, and our competitors couldn't be happier about it.

This is patently stupid policy. 

We should be lowering costs for families and outcompeting China, and I'll keep fighting to do both.
https://t.co/uFWwkdxafo

The scope of frontier model misalignment is staggering. The past month has exposed how public admissions are just the tip of the iceberg.

AI agents have colluded, escaped their sandboxes, hacked other companies, meddled with government portals — and that's just the ones we know about.

The need for enforceable guardrails from Congress is undeniable, including independent monitors and industry-wide standards to safeguard against AI's greatest risks.

quoted.text:
SCOOP: OpenAI, Anthropic and security researchers are investigating tens of thousands of incidents - not dozens - in which their frontier models took steps that outside evaluators would consider problematic, sources told Axios.

The sheer volume of incidents found in our reporting indicate that the problem is orders of magnitude more complex than what is currently publicly known and disclosed.

The findings also raise questions about what level of control anyone working on AI development can expect to have over their own technology, and whether these kinds of incidents are becoming synonymous with frontier deployment.

It’s great to see the Hudson River Tunnel of the Gateway Project officially underway! 🚞 
Once complete, this is going to be a game changer for New Jersey commuters, regional jobs, and our nation’s economy. Thanks to all who worked to get us here. I can’t wait to see the tunnel’s progress.

quoted.text:
The first tunnel boring machine is officially digging into the Palisades Cliffs, marking a major milestone for the Gateway Tunnel.

Nearly 200,000 passengers depend on the current century-old tunnel every day, and our region generates 20% of our nation’s GDP. The Gateway Tunnel will deliver the modern, reliable infrastructure New Jersey commuters deserve and our economy depends on.

Back in Congress, they called me the “tunnel-obsessed Congresswoman” because I fought tooth and nail for Gateway. Now, I’m the “tunnel-obsessed Governor,” and I’ll keep fighting to make sure the nation's most urgent infrastructure project gets built.

Congratulations to Safe Streets Belvedere on 379 consecutive days without a homicide. That is more than a statistic. It represents lives saved, families kept whole, and a community proving that violence is not inevitable. This milestone belongs to everyone doing the work: the violence interrupters, Mayor Scott and his team, MONSE, LifeBridge Health’s Center for Hope, law enforcement, prosecutors, community and faith organizations, and most importantly, the neighbors who call this community home. It takes an all-of-the-above approach: prevention, intervention, accountability, opportunity, treatment, federal investment, and neighbors looking out for one another.

Baltimore’s legacy is bigger than the violence others too often use to define us. Our story is one of people caring for one another, building neighborhoods, and refusing to give up on each other. Celebrate this moment, but don’t stop. Keep working. Keep believing in Baltimore. And most of all, keep loving one another. Congratulations, Safe Streets Belvedere. 379 days and counting.

Thank you for your faith, your kindness, and your prayers.
